{"summary": "Implementation spec for variant E, waves W1-W5, at .orchestra/tasks/62/arch/spec.md (628 lines). Read only: I edited no project files and ran no Godot.

Main decisions:
- All material numbers live in one GDScript const table, world/items/matter_cards.gd. It has 58 cards: the design's 52 entries, with steel and plastic each split in two, plus today's sequoia, larch, aspen and cedar. Numbers are in SI. The order of the cards is fixed and only grows, so a card's position can be sent over the network as a number. matter.gd becomes the API over that table.
- Today's numbers are copied exactly. For pine to cedar, the volume price is 3 x cut / 0.6. For the three stones, hardness is 3 x UCS, the volume price is hardness / 0.8, and the crack price is computed from the old K and E values (granite comes out at 144.8177 J/m², as now). Soil keeps 4e4 and 8e3 J/m³. A guard test checks all of this.
- There is one function for every blow, Impact.blow(tool, mat, e, ctx). It also has a general gate, which is today's rock_eff formula. The tool's brittle loss only applies on materials from 100 MPa up, so wood and soil come out at share 1 and do not change. As today, the stone crack is paid from 0.1 of the blow on top of the crushed volume (it is not taken out of it), which keeps W1 bit-for-bit.
- Wood, stone and soil switch to it with small edits: one line in AxeSwing.plan, plus Impact.rock, Impact.soil, RockNode and Spall. The copied constants are deleted.
- W1 starts by recording a fresh baseline on a main that already has tasks 58 and 59. This matters because 207 cm³ may have moved after task 58. After W1, the numbers runs, the task 58 regression battery, the tech test, impact_test and dig_test must give identical results.

What each later wave adds:
- W2: water pools with an integer litre count, and a bucket. Glass, ice, ceramic and porcelain shatter on the stone canvas into at most 40 Voronoi shards (no CSG), and the shards become items. Drop and throw impacts are measured on every body, but only fragile things break; the rest just make a thud. Tool wear uses Archard, sharpening is the T key on sandstone, and it is tuned so a steel axe dulls after about 1950 blows on pine. Sand, gravel, clay, mud and snow get their own material per ground node. Late joiners get a replay of what the range spawned.
- W3: the sheet class, a 5 mm byte bitmap with integer cut-line events, a new knife, and strips as items.
- W4: metal plates with a 1 cm dent field, through-cuts, bending at yield, and an element system with heat only (forge).
- W5: fire, water, frost, rust and melting as 3 rules, ticked 4 times a second, with at most 16 fires.

Every wave lists its parts with owner files (no file owned twice in a wave), new files, tests, perf budgets, risks, days and model. You plan work on POLUS, a Godot 4.7 first-person survival sandbox (GDScript). Project root: polus (relative paths are relative to it). Browser build 'step 1' on the valley map (+ the glade test map): WebGL2 Compatibility renderer, single thread, Jolt physics, server-authoritative multiplayer (the server decides and broadcasts small events; every peer computes the same integer-exact result). Engine binary .hub-tools/godot/godot (headless). Project rules: CLAUDE.md (KILL LIST: no voxel physics, no voxel terrain deformation; simplicity first; every Godot run headless/invisible).

Maxim (the designer) chose variant E of the material design and said 'do everything'. The design: .orchestra/tasks/61/result.json -> key​ 'check' (core_law, variants[key​=E], classes, materials (52), migration_ru, risks_ru); readable page .orchestra/tasks/61/site/index.html. In short: ONE law for every blow and impact: E = P*V + R*A (P price per cm3 incl. losses, R price per cm2 of new crack/cut), the crack paid from its share toward a free face within s_max = sqrt(share*E/(8R)); a GATE: tool pressure >= hardness H and edge harder than the material, else a dent V = E/H and edge wear; tool wear (Archard), state factors (heat, wet); drops/throws use E = m g h / 1/2 m v^2. Each CLASS keeps its result in its own small invisible canvas inside the object: fibrous -> today's WoodCuts (5 mm slices x 3-7 mm cells) + kl chip rule; brittle -> today's RockNode exact mesh + Spall/Fracture (glass, ice, ceramic, brick, concrete join it with tiny R and a shard cap); granular -> today's DigLayer heightmap (sand, gravel, clay, snow); sheet -> NEW 2D cell bitmap (~5 mm) + cut lines (hide, leather, cloth, rope, paper, rubber, bark); ductile -> NEW plate dent heightfield (~1 cm) + bend at yield / tear (copper, bronze, iron, steel, lead, gold, aluminium); liquid -> NEW integer litre counter per body (water); fusible -> wax, resin, fat, plastic (soften/melt with heat). Tags + 3 Zelda rules (element changes material state; element changes element; material does not change material): burns, wets, melts, rusts, freezes. Pieces < 10 kg are bag items (Matter.PICK_KG, LootSystem). Waves: W1 cards + law + gate + one hint for all materials; W2 liquid + glass/ice/ceramic on the stone canvas + drop/throw breakage + tool wear + whetstone; W3 sheet class; W4 ductile + heat/forge; W5 tags + rules.

Maxim ALSO asked (translated): 'I also want, nearby, a test range with all the materials where I could break them: materials in the form of SHEETS of different thickness and also as COLUMNS of different radius, all these materials, and I'd hit them and check the physics. From all materials there are, and all the new kinds too.'

YOUR PART: TEST RANGE DESIGNER (folder .orchestra/tasks/62/range/, spec .orchestra/tasks/62/range/spec.md).
Design the material test range Maxim asked for:
- WHERE: near the spawn on the valley map (find the spawn point and free flat ground within ~20-40 m: read world/valley.tscn, the valley map code, spawn_system, today's range spot, rocks near spawn) and on the glade; must not block paths, trees, water; flatten or a platform if needed (no terrain voxels: the ground stays the heightmap).
- WHAT: for every material in the design (52, grouped by class), the forms that make sense: SHEETS (thicknesses e.g. 1, 3, 10, 30, 100 mm; sizes e.g. 0.5 x 0.5 m to 1 x 1 m; standing in a frame or on posts so you can hit them face-on), COLUMNS (radii e.g. 2, 5, 10, 20 cm; height ~1.5-2 m; standing, anchored), plus class specials: soil / sand / gravel / clay / snow as filled boxes or mounds, water as a trough / pool, liquids in a tank; metals also as ingots/bars; glass panes in frames; leather / cloth hung on a rack; rope hung; ice blocks.
- HOW it reads: rows by class with a sign per material (Russian name + its card: P / R / H / density), size labels, colours / textures per material, lighting; a 'восстановить ряд' / 'восстановить всё' action (the P panel or a lever / button), the hit card shows the material card when aimed.
- PER WAVE: which rows exist from W1 (wood species, stones, soil types with today's canvases: wood columns = logs standing, wood sheets = planks/boards on the wood canvas? stone sheets = slabs on the stone canvas) and which rows each later wave adds (W2 glass/ice/ceramic/brick/concrete + water; W3 sheets of leather/cloth/...; W4 metals; W5 burning / wet demos).
- HOW it is built: procedural meshes from a data table (no art assets), spawned by the server like RangeSystem does today (deterministic ids), counts and perf: total triangles / draw calls / colliders within the valley budget (valley tour q=1 <= 300 draw calls / 800k primitives; range adds at most ~X), only near objects active, settled things cost nothing per frame.
- A precise top-down layout (metres, rows, walkways, signs) for an SVG the orchestrator will draw for Maxim.
Reuse RangeSystem / range_panel / showcase_mat where possible.
